picks.editorial_note: A combined $1.1B+ commitment from Georgia Tech and Emory is one of the largest university AI investments announced this year, positioning Georgia as a national AI hub and signaling how much capital research universities are now willing to deploy on AI infrastructure and talent.
picks.title: Georgia Tech and Emory Invest More Than $1B in AI to Drive State’s Jobs, Economic Growth

picks.editorial_note: A White House-announced 15-university, 10-state computing consortium marks a significant federal push to regionalize AI supercomputing capacity, reflecting a deliberate policy strategy to broaden access beyond a handful of elite AI hubs.
picks.title: UK partners with regional universities in super intelligence computing consortium

picks.editorial_note: SLAC leading a DOE Genesis Mission project to apply autonomous AI-driven discovery to catalysis research could accelerate breakthroughs in energy-relevant chemistry, exemplifying the federal government's flagship strategy for AI-accelerated science.
picks.title: SLAC to lead a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project for Super Intelligence (SI)-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis

picks.editorial_note: Georgia Tech's $20M NSF-funded Nexus supercomputer, opened to researchers nationwide in partnership with UIUC, expands shared national AI compute infrastructure at a time when GPU access is a major bottleneck for academic research.
picks.title: Georgia Tech Opens Supercomputer to Researchers Nationwide

picks.editorial_note: Phase II DOE Genesis Mission funding for Berkeley Lab's MOAT-Core project applies AI to particle accelerator design and operation, advancing a key tool for fundamental physics research with direct federal backing.
picks.title: Super Intelligence for Particle Accelerators Gets Another Boost

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's SPIRE project to build fully autonomous 'self-driving laboratories' using AI agents and robots represents a notable step toward automating experimental science itself, not just data analysis.
picks.title: SLAC leads new project to build the self-driving laboratory of the future

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's two new Genesis Mission awards apply AI to microelectronics and quantum information science, areas critical to both future computing hardware and national competitiveness in strategic technologies.
picks.title: Fermilab to lead two new Genesis Mission awards to accelerate development of microelectronics and quantum

picks.editorial_note: A CWRU-linked startup's optical computing chips, which use light instead of electronic circuits, target one of AI's biggest looming constraints — runaway energy consumption — with a credible technical approach rather than incremental efficiency tweaks.
picks.title: A CWRU entrepreneur studied invisibility cloaks. Now he’s working to cut AI’s energy use | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University

picks.editorial_note: TUM spinout RobCo reaching unicorn status with a robotics platform for industrial automation shows academic AI/robotics research translating directly into major commercial value and job-creating enterprise.
picks.title: RobCo: TUM’s 24th unicorn

picks.editorial_note: An R&D 100 Award for the multi-lab Persistent DynAMICS project recognizes a working AI-enhanced facility-monitoring system now in real-world national-security use, a rare case of lab AI research reaching deployed, award-winning maturity.
picks.title: NNSS collaborates on LANL's R&D 100 Award-winning Persistent DynAMICS project - Nevada National Security Site
